prompt: The fallen spine of a colossal wrecked warship as a compact sculpture on a solid rounded mound of desert sand: a massive thick armoured keel beam rising out of the mound at a shallow angle, a row of huge thick curved rib frames standing up from it like the skeleton of a whale, a few heavy torn hull plates riveted between the ribs. Welded directly onto the high end of the keel is a chunky relay post: a solid boxy weatherproof equipment housing with a short thick mast, three short crossbars and a small dish, all heavy and solidly attached. Sun-bleached, chunky, solid salvage-desert metal; no thin wires, no separate objects. Isolated 3D model render on a plain uniform medium-grey studio background, the whole object fully in frame with generous margin, three-quarter view from slightly above, soft even studio lighting, no cast shadow, no text, no lettering, no logos, no people. Crisp hard-surface modelling with bold, clearly separated parts and a strong readable silhouette: chunky forms and clean edges, no clutter, no hanging moss, no dangling wires.
